To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the formylation of 3-substituted thiophene derivatives proceeds via a mechanism involving the formation of an intermediate, and the reaction is accelerated in aprotic solvents and is slowed down in protic solvents.

the formylation of the thiophene derivatives was found to be an S _{E} 2 reaction, and the reaction rate was found to increase with increasing electron-withdrawing ability of the substituents in the para position.
The formylation reaction of thiophene and derivatives in the presence phosphorus oxychlorides is a second order reaction with respect to the substrate.

the formylation of heterocyclic compounds with N,N-diethylformamide.
the formylation of aromatic compounds in the presence of a strong Lewis acid and an amide.

the formylation reaction of thiophene with N,N-dimehtylformamide is a nucleophilic reaction.

the reaction is of the first order in the substrate, of the zero order in the condensing agent, of the second order in the solvent, of the first order with respect to the solvent and of the zero order with respect to hydrogen chloride.
